key_insight: A versatile two-layer model (VTLM) compresses 3D microchannel heat-sink thermohydraulics into two coupled 2D fields while preserving in-plane geometry and key channel-height effects.
engineering_relevance: This enables much faster design-space screening of microchannel heat sinks across many geometries and operating conditions without fully resolving 3D flow.
method: Uses two coupled 2D fields for fluid and solid heat transfer.
Adds hydraulic and thermal closure relations to represent unresolved channel-height physics.
Calibrates closures from representative channel geometry, flow-development state, and fin configuration.
evidence_signal: The VTLM was benchmarked against 3D reference simulations over wide ranges of channel aspect ratios, operating conditions, and fin arrangements, and showed improved agreement versus prior two-layer models.
watch_item: Accuracy depends strongly on flow-development condition and channel aspect ratio, so the screening guideline should be applied cautiously outside the examined straight-channel and abrupt-width-change cases.
paper_title: Versatile two-layer model for thermohydraulic prediction of microchannel heat sinks
